title: Understanding Your Annual Salary: Minimum Wage Australia 2026 and the 38-Hour Week
description: Convert your hourly rate to annual pay with our guide. Includes minimum wage Australia 2026 figures, tax brackets, super guarantee, and fortnightly estimates for a 38-hour week.
salarySummary: For a standard 38-hour week, your annual gross pay is your hourly rate multiplied by 38 hours per week and then by 52 weeks.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week (typically 38 for full-time) and then by 52 weeks. For example, $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,254.80 per year. This gives your gross annual pay before tax and super.

faqs.q: What is the minimum wage in Australia for 2026?
faqs.a: From 1 July 2026, the national minimum wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1004.90 per week for a 38-hour week. Casual employees receive 25% loading, making it $33.05 per hour. These rates are set by the Fair Work Commission.

faqs.q: How much tax and super will I pay on my annual salary?
faqs.a: Tax depends on your income using the 2026–27 resident tax brackets (nil to $18,200, then 15%, 30%, 37%, 45%) plus 2% Medicare levy. Super is 12% of your ordinary earnings paid on top by your employer, up to the $270,830 cap. For the minimum wage, estimated annual tax is about $7,867 and super about $6,270.

bodyMarkdown:
## How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay

Whether you're negotiating a salary offer or planning your household budget, understanding how your hourly rate translates to annual, fortnightly, and weekly pay is essential. The standard formula used across Australia is: hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks. For full-time employees, the typical week is 38 hours, as defined by the Fair Work Ombudsman. This guide uses that 38-hour benchmark to give you consistent estimates. If your hours differ, simply substitute your own weekly hours.

### The 38-Hour Week and Fortnightly Pay

A 38-hour week is the standard full-time hours under most modern awards and the National Employment Standards. To find your weekly gross pay, multiply your hourly rate by 38. For a fortnightly pay cycle, double that weekly amount. For example, if you earn the **minimum wage australia 2026** of $26.44 per hour, your weekly gross is $1004.90 (38 × $26.44) and your fortnightly gross is $2009.80. These are before any deductions for tax or super.

### Annual Gross Pay

Multiplying your weekly pay by 52 gives your annual gross salary. Using the minimum wage example: $1004.90 × 52 = $52,254.80 per year. This calculation assumes you work every week of the year with no unpaid leave. If you take unpaid leave, your actual annual income will be lower. The formula is simple: hourly × hours per week × 52.

### Minimum Wage Australia 2026

The Fair Work Commission reviews the national minimum wage each financial year. From 1 July 2026, the **minimum wage australia 2026** is $26.44 per hour, or $1004.90 per week for a 38-hour week. Casual employees receive an additional 25% loading, making their minimum rate $33.05 per hour. This loading compensates for the lack of paid leave such as annual leave and personal leave. Note that the National Minimum Wage is the legal minimum for employees not covered by an award or agreement. Many workers are covered by industry or occupation awards that set higher minimum rates. Always check your specific award or agreement. For more details, see our [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page.

### Award Rates vs National Minimum Wage

The National Minimum Wage is the floor, but most industries have award rates set by the Fair Work Commission. These rates vary by classification, experience, and role. For example, a retail employee may have a higher base rate than the national minimum. When using our [the timesheet](/), you enter your base hourly rate. If you are a casual, tick the box to add 25% casual loading. Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading. The tool will apply the loading on top.

### Superannuation Guarantee

Employers must pay superannuation on top of your ordinary earnings. From 2026–27, the super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is paid separately by your employer into a super fund. For the minimum wage example, the annual super contribution would be 12% of $52,254.80 = $6,270.58, assuming no cap is exceeded. If your annual earnings exceed $270,830, super is only paid on the first $270,830. Learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Tax on Your Annual Salary

Your annual gross pay is subject to income tax and the Medicare levy. For 2026–27, the resident tax rates are:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

The Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. For a full-time worker on the minimum wage, annual gross of $52,254.80 falls into the 30% bracket after the tax-free threshold. The estimated tax (including Medicare) would be approximately $7,867 (using the 2026–27 scale and 2025–26 Medicare reduction thresholds as per the disclaimer). For a more precise estimate, use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator.

### Fortnightly and Weekly Estimates

If you are paid fortnightly, your gross pay is your weekly amount times two. For the minimum wage, that's $2009.80. After tax and Medicare, your fortnightly take-home would be roughly $1,700 (estimate). Remember that tax is withheld by your employer based on the tax tables, so your actual net pay may vary. The fortnightly figure is useful for budgeting if you are paid every two weeks.

### Average Weekly Earnings Comparison

The Australian Bureau of Statistics publishes Average Weekly Earnings. For May 2026, full-time adult ordinary time earnings averaged $2083.7 per week. This is an average across all full-time employees, not a median for any specific job. Your own pay may be higher or lower depending on your industry, experience, and location. For more context, see our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page.

### Using the Timesheet Tool

Our [the timesheet](/) tool allows you to enter your base hourly rate and choose whether to include casual loading. It then calculates your weekly, fortnightly, and annual gross pay, along with estimated tax and super. It assumes a 38-hour week unless you change the hours. The results are estimates only. For detailed award rates, refer to our [pay guides](/blog) and [reference tables](/data).

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For job-specific rates, see [job pay](/topics/job-pay). For casual loading details, see [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading). And for conversion help, see [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion).
